description: Returns the service's current date, its IANA timezone, and the current ISO week with its start and end dates and page path. Call this first to resolve relative dates such as "today" or "three weeks ago"; the server accepts only explicit YYYY-MM-DD dates. The result also includes the household profile: five sections (household, food, kitchen, planning, other), each with its text and revision. Read the profile before planning. Takes no arguments.

An empty result is a normal response; widen the date range yourself if appropriate. Use get_meal with a result's id for the full recipe.

description: Use this whenever the user asks what to buy or what is on the shopping list for a day, such as today. description: Creates or replaces ONE ISO week. This is a full replacement within that week: any existing day, meal, step, shopping list, category, item or prep session that is not in the submitted document is deleted. To change one thing, call get_week, edit the document, and submit all of it. Other weeks are never touched. Use client-generated lowercase UUIDs for new records and keep existing ids to preserve them. Optional values must be explicit nulls; array order is stored order. Every prep session needs a weekday, 1-7 (Monday=1) or null; a null weekday shows the session on no day. To create a week that has no saved plan yet, omit expectedRevision; if a plan is already saved, this returns revision_conflict. To replace a saved week, pass the revision from get_week as expectedRevision; a mismatch returns revision_conflict, after which you must fetch the week again and reconcile. There is no force option. The whole save is one transaction: an invalid document changes nothing. Returns the committed week and its new revision.

document.description: The complete week. Everything not listed here is deleted from the stored week.

days.description: Day records, at most one per weekday. A weekday that is absent has no day record.

weekday.description: 1 (Monday) ..= 7 of the session's week, or null: the session is shown on no day.

id.description: Canonical lowercase UUID; must equal the stored id when replacing an existing week.

expectedRevision.description: The revision from get_week, to replace that saved week. Omit it to create a week that has no saved plan yet; null also creates.

isoWeek.description: ISO week number of the week to save, 1 to 53.

isoYear.description: ISO week-numbering year of the week to save.

title: Save a complete week

description: Use this to record lasting household knowledge in one section of the household profile that get_context returns: household (people, portions, dietary restrictions), food (likes, dislikes, cuisines), kitchen (equipment, storage, limitations), planning (cooking time, shopping, budget, leftovers, batch prep) or other. Save only what the user stated or confirmed, never preferences you inferred. To bootstrap the profile from a conversation, show the proposed text to the user and save it only after they approve. Circumstances that apply to one week only belong in that week (its subtitle or a reminder, via save_week), not in the profile. This replaces the whole section text, so to add a fact, start from the section's current text from get_context and submit all of it. Pass that section's revision as expectedRevision; if the section changed since, this returns revision_conflict, after which call get_context again, reconcile with the user and resubmit. There is no force option. Plain text, at most 4,000 characters; other sections and all weeks are untouched. Returns the saved section and its new revision.
